rows.medi_said: So الواجب عندو تلات سو-- أسول-- أو-- Hold on. أسئلة.
rows.amal_said: صح. فيو ثلاث أسئلة. ... فيو، in it. ... It doesn't have. There's in it.
rows.why: He used عندو (it has) for a thing containing questions; Amal recast to فيو and explained 'It doesn't have. There's in it'; he took it ('instead of عندي، فيو').

rows.medi_said: Intira, uh, raha... tin, uh... tinnis be mayi.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. Happy with me. ... Happy from, from something I did. ... minni.
rows.why: enbasat takes min (happy from something I did); he said ma3i (with me), Amal said Mm-mm and gave minni, he agreed 'I did say mayi'.
rows.english: You will be happy with me.

rows.medi_said: أنا بحكي--
rows.amal_said: وأنا؟
rows.why: Telling about last night he started in the present (ba7ki); after Amal's 'وأنا؟' he switched to past حكيت - her line may only be an echo, so low.
rows.english: I spoke a lot of Arabic.

rows.medi_said: و الـ-- وال بنات الـ-- بنات و-- أو ولاد، أمها أو أبوها.
rows.amal_said: ولاد أمها. ... أوه، عمها وعمتها. Cuz ولاد أمها are أخوتها.
rows.why: He meant aunts and uncles ('Aunts and uncles') but said 'children of her mother or father' (= her siblings); Amal pointed that out and gave عمها وعمتها (sheet: uncle (paternal) | 3am; aunt (paternal) | 3ammeh), he repeated amama u ameta.

rows.medi_said: uh, huwe,
rows.amal_said: هم مات؟
rows.chat: humme yefhammu kter bas lamma laazem ye7ku
rows.why: Talking about the cousins (they) he said huwe (he), also at 06:42 'hu-huwe bif-bifhamu'; Amal's 'هم...؟' (engine 'هم مات', = humme?) prompted and he switched to هم at 07:38.

rows.medi_said: their ahel hom, uh, yehku inglisi ma hom.
rows.why: Plain present habit 'their parents speak English with them' needs b- (bye7ku, as her chat writes); she let it pass.
rows.english: Their parents speak English with them.

rows.medi_said: anhom walad hon hu, bifikru el lugha muhim ilhom.
rows.chat: bas humme 3indhom wlaad han u beyfakkru el-lu8a ra7 tkoon muhemma ilhom fi el-musta2bal
rows.why: He means they have kids (plural, chat wlaad) but the engine wrote walad (one boy); may be the engine, so low.

rows.medi_said: bifikru el lugha muhim ilhom. ... Language is gonna be important, yeah.
rows.amal_said: So it's going to be. ... راح.
rows.right: beyfakkru el-lu8a ra7 tkoon muhemma ilhom
rows.why: He meant 'language is going to be important' (said so in English) but left out the future; Amal's English 'So it's going to be' and 'راح' prompted rah fikun.
rows.english: They think the language is going to be important for them.

rows.medi_said: Uh, rah fikun. ... Going to be rah.
rows.amal_said: Yeah، بس لغة as well.
rows.why: لغة is feminine so the adjective must be muhemma; Amal's 'بس لغة as well' prompted, he said 'Oh, it's feminine. Rah fikun muhema'.

rows.medi_said: Oh, it's feminine. Rah fikun muhema ilhom.
rows.why: With feminine لغة the be-verb is tkoon (her chat); he kept fikun/ykoon after fixing the adjective; could be the engine.
rows.english: It's going to be important for them.

rows.medi_said: il modara. No, modara is present... moraja. ... Mak. Does it have a K in it? ... maba nasito.
rows.amal_said: Do you remember the word for future؟ ... مـ-مس... مستقبل.
rows.why: Amal asked for the word for future; he tried modara (a grammar term for present) and moraja, could not find it, she prompted مـ-مس and gave مستقبل (sheet: future | Musta2bal).

rows.medi_said: How do I say-- Do I know how to say adults? I don't know how to say adults.
rows.amal_said: Just we say the big ones يعني the big.
rows.why: He asked how to say adults; Amal told him el-kbaar (the big ones).

rows.medi_said: Shwe min kbar, uh, libisna costume bas kul il zgar.
rows.amal_said: So لبسوا. ليش؟
rows.chat: shwai min el-kbaar ma lebsu lebset Haloween bas kul el-z8aar lebsu
rows.why: Subject is the adults (they) but he used the we-form libisna (also at 10:31 'Ma libisna'); Amal gave لبسوا, he asked 'It would be لبسوا?' and she confirmed.
rows.english: Some of the adults wore costumes but all the kids...

rows.medi_said: Shwe min kbar, uh, libisna costume
rows.why: The known group 'some of the adults' needs el- (min el-kbaar, her chat); he said it right elsewhere (il kbar), she did not voice it.

rows.medi_said: Shwe min kbar, uh, libisna costume bas kul il zgar.
rows.chat: shwai min el-kbaar ma lebsu lebset Haloween bas kul el-z8aar lebsu
rows.why: His point (adults did not dress up, but all the kids did; 10:31 'Ma libisna') needs ma; this restart dropped it; her chat has ma lebsu.

rows.medi_said: il kbar libsu costume bas...
rows.amal_said: How about you say a Halloween outfit. We don't really have a costume.
rows.why: He used English costume (not on her sheet); Amal said Arabic has no word and offered 'a Halloween outfit' (lebset Haloween) - a new phrase, so tier 0.

rows.medi_said: Okay. Uh, libsa Halloween. ... Libsa, right?
rows.amal_said: لبست.
rows.why: Feminine first word of an idafa takes -t; Amal recast libsa -> لبست, he repeated Libsit and explained 'because you're describing Halloween'.

rows.medi_said: كان حلووات كتير. كانوا حلوات كتير. ... كل، كل ولاد.
rows.amal_said: Are they all كلهم بنات؟ ... لأ، عاد صغار بس حلوين قول حلوات.
rows.why: For a mixed group of kids the plural adjective is حلوين; Amal asked 'are they all girls?' then said حلوين, he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: كل حدا، آآ، جابوا واحد أكلة.
rows.amal_said: So all everyone as in everybody. ... بس now I'm describing one. So jab أو jabu. ... Cos I'm saying person.
rows.why: kul 7ada (everyone) is singular so the verb is jaab; Amal explained 'I'm describing one... jab', he said 'Oh, you're right. جاب'.

rows.medi_said: كل حدا جاب واحد أكل، أكلة. No، واحدة أكلة.
rows.amal_said: آ، واحدة is an adjective. So what do where do I put it؟
rows.why: Adjective goes after the noun; Amal named it ('واحدة is an adjective, where do I put it?'), he fixed to أكلة واحدة (first said واحد أكلة at 13:08).

rows.medi_said: كل عيلتها، آآ، طلبوني. ... طلبوا عليّ؟ ... طلبوا لي؟ مني.
rows.amal_said: طلبوه. ... No. They requested. meaning.
rows.chat: kul 3aieltha talabu minni  enno ajeeb kabaab
rows.why: talab (ask/request) takes min for the person; he put the person on the verb (طلبوني) then tried عليّ / لي; Amal questioned it and said 'No. They requested', he got طلبوا مني.
rows.english: Her whole family asked me (to bring kebab).

rows.medi_said: طلبوا مني، آآ، إنه جبت kebab. ... supreme؟ ولا just جيب؟ فجيب؟
rows.amal_said: إنه to bring. ... أجيب kebab.
rows.chat: kul 3aieltha talabu minni  enno ajeeb kabaab
rows.why: After 'they asked me that' the asked-for action is a bare I-form present (ajeeb), not past jebet or the command jeeb; Amal said 'إنه to bring' then gave أجيب, he repeated it.
rows.english: They asked me to bring kebab.
rows.proposed_rule: After a request (talab min ... enno) the asked-for action is a bare present verb with the doer's person, not past or a command: talabu minni enno ajeeb kabaab

rows.medi_said: شو، شو الكلمة spinach؟
rows.amal_said: سبانخ.
rows.why: He asked the word for spinach; Amal gave سبانخ (sheet: spinach | sabane5).

rows.medi_said: بيضة. ... مثل بيضة like eggs and cheese, right؟
rows.amal_said: لا، لا، لا، لا. It's a type of cheese. نوع من الجبنة، جبنة بيضا.
rows.why: Amal asked about الجبنة البيضا (white cheese); he heard بيضة (egg) and asked if it meant eggs and cheese; she said no, it is white cheese.

rows.medi_said: أسألها أسر مارا الجاي.
rows.why: 'next time' is noun+adjective phrase with el- on both (el-marra el-jaay, her chat); engine wrote مارا without el-, may be mishearing.

rows.medi_said: يوم الثلاث،
rows.amal_said: No.
rows.why: Today (2026-11-02) is Monday; he said Tuesday (sheet: tuesday | Yoam el-tulata), Amal said No and he gave يوم الاثنين.

rows.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم. ... أنا بأسب، أنا بأسب لهم
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Mm-mm. And about it was I get angry.
rows.why: For 'upset for them' he used ba3asseb (engine بأسب; sheet: i get angry | Ana ba3asseb); Amal said Mm-mm and that his word is 'I get angry'; he moved to داية it = tdaaya2et (sheet: i feel upset about / for someone | Ana batDaaya2 3ala).

rows.medi_said: أنا بأسب، أنا بأسب لهم
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. I got.
rows.why: The sentence is past ('I got upset') but he used a present verb; Amal stressed 'I got', he said 'Oh, you're right' and used the past.

rows.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them.
rows.why: tdaaya2 for someone takes 3ala; he said منهم then لهم, Amal said Mm-mm to both; he reasoned to ala and she said Saħħ to Alayhom.

rows.medi_said: Alayhom ala...
rows.amal_said: No, you don't need anything. If you do-- If you would want to put something, it would be in, in anything.
rows.why: He started to put ala before 'the end of the movie'; Amal said no preposition is needed; he was mid-sentence, so low.
rows.english: at the end of the movie

rows.medi_said: akher. No, tahet. ... Akher.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. La saħħ. ... Shu yammi taħet. It's not taħet.
rows.why: For 'end of the movie' he switched to taħet (under; sheet: down / under | Ta7t); Amal said 'It's not taħet', he said 'Under' and went back to akher.

rows.medi_said: أنا جاوبت على أغلب من-- أغلب الـ، أغلب السؤال، or as-, uh, أسعيد، أسئ، أسئلة،
rows.amal_said: Il. Saħħ.
rows.why: a8lab takes el- + plural noun directly (sheet: A8lab + el + noun); he said أغلب من then أسئلة without el-; Amal's 'Il' prompted the el- (Medi at 28:43: 'I said أغلب من and you corrected me').
rows.english: I answered most of the questions today.

rows.medi_said: من الـ آخر than the end, right? ... الـ آخر-- ... Is it آخره؟
rows.amal_said: The end of it. ... Just it. ... صح، آخره.
rows.chat: awal el-ijtemaa3 kaan aswa2 min aa5ro
rows.why: 'the end of it' is آخره with the pronoun ending, no el-; Amal prompted 'The end of it... Just it' until he got آخره.
rows.english: worse than the end of it

rows.medi_said: منيح بس ما حبيت الـ آخرو.
rows.amal_said: No ال. Why? ... Why no ال؟
rows.chat: awal el-felem mnaa7 bas mnee7 bas maa 7abbait aa5ro
rows.why: A word with a pronoun ending is already definite, so no el- (aa5ro); Amal said 'No ال. Why?', he answered 'cause it's conjugated'.
rows.english: but I didn't like the end of it

rows.medi_said: غير تاني. No، إشي غير من هم.
rows.amal_said: غير إشي، ليش؟
rows.why: 8eir goes before the noun; Amal recast غير إشي and asked why, he said 'غير always comes before the noun... the wrong word'.
rows.english: I asked for something different from them.

rows.medi_said: Would it be مواسف here or would it be ياسر؟
rows.amal_said: بيعصب بس كان أو كانوا cuz أخبار is multiple news.
rows.why: He did not know the word for 'angering' (asked at 39:12 'Isn't it مواسف' = m3asseb, Amal: 'is angry, but angering') and asked again; she gave بيعصب (sheet: i get angry / make someone angry | Ana ba3asseb).

rows.medi_said: uh, كان angering.
rows.amal_said: بيعصب بس كان أو كانوا cuz أخبار is multiple news.
rows.why: أخبار is plural so the verb is kaanu; Amal said 'كان أو كانوا cuz أخبار is multiple news', he took it ('is it plural?... you're right').

rows.medi_said: أنا قرأت الأخبار، أوّل الصباح، أو بيعصبوا.
rows.amal_said: أمم، they were.
rows.chat: ana qara2et el-a5baar awal el-subu7 u kaanu bey3assbu
rows.why: In the past the state needs kaan + present (kaanu bey3assbu); Amal said 'they were', he added كانو.

rows.medi_said: Okay. الـ حفلة. Um, راح,
rows.amal_said: الحفلة؟ [تضحك] I wish I would be a حفلة.
rows.why: He said الحفلة (the party) for the war; Amal echoed it laughing, he then said 'Oh my God. الحرب' (sheet: war | 7arb).
rows.english: The war is going to get worse.

rows.medi_said: الحرب راح, راح يسير أسوأ.
rows.amal_said: أممم، آه، sharp is
rows.chat: ana bazonn enno el-7arb ra7 tseer aswa2
rows.why: حرب is a hidden-feminine noun (bucket A18 names war) so the verb is tseer; Amal's 'harb is...' (engine 'sharp is') prompted and he said راح تصير أسوأ.
rows.english: The war is going to get worse.

rows.medi_said: لما أنا أطلع الطبيعة
rows.amal_said: أطلع at.
rows.chat: el-ishi el-mufaddal 3indi lamma ana at6alla3 3ala el-6abi3a
rows.why: 'look at' is at6alla3 3ala (sheet: i look at | Ana bat6alla3 3ala); Amal prompted 'أطلع at', he said 'أتطلع على الطبيعة' and 'I forgot to say it'.

rows.medi_said: إشي المفضل عندي. ... Or المفضل إشي عندي.
rows.amal_said: Where do you put the Ls? ... Where is the other L? You have another L. Where do you put it?
rows.why: mufaddal after the noun matches its el-, so el-ishi el-mufaddal (her chat); Amal asked twice where the other L goes; he kept إشي المفضل.

rows.medi_said: إنه or اللي...
rows.amal_said: You don't need anything actually just. ... Cuz it's is.
rows.why: He put إنه / اللي for 'is' in 'my favorite thing is when...'; Amal said no word is needed 'cuz it's is'.
rows.english: My favorite thing is when I look at nature.

rows.medi_said: No, your صحابك تانيين.
rows.amal_said: close. ... التاني.
rows.why: After a definite noun (pronoun ending) taani takes el-; Amal said 'close' then التاني and explained 'صحابك is definitive'.

rows.medi_said: um, عائلتي, my other family, عائلت- عائلتي, it would be التاني.
rows.amal_said: Yes. التانية.
rows.why: عيلة is feminine so 'other' is التانية; Amal recast it, he repeated التانية.

rows.medi_said: هذي أول مرة أول يومي هون.
rows.amal_said: هذا.
rows.why: يوم is masculine so 'this' is هذا; Amal recast هذا right after.
rows.english: This is my first day here.

rows.medi_said: هذي أول مرة أول يومي هون. ... هذي أول اليومي هون.
rows.amal_said: أول يومي is what? ... No. What does أول يومي mean? ... No.
rows.why: awal + a possessive noun means 'the beginning of my day'; Amal said No several times and led him to يومي الأول (55:30) and هذا أول يوم إلي (56:08); his 53:43 أول اليومي is the same moment.
rows.english: This is my first day here.
